(i) If m > 2, m ̸≡r (mod 2) , and p ≡ r (mod m) with r ⩾ −m/ 2, then p−1∑ k=0 (−1)km (r/m k ) m ≡ 0 (mod p3). (ii) If p ≡ r (mod 2 m) with r ⩾ −m, then p−1∑ k=0 (−1)k (r/m k ) 2n+1 ≡ 0 (mod p2) for all n = 1 , . . . , m − 1. (iii) For any prime p and positive integer n, we have νp (n−1∑ k=0 (−1/ (p + 1) k ) p+1) ⩾ cp ⌊νp(n) + 1 ⌋ , where cp =      1 if p = 2 , 3 if p = 3 , 5 if p ⩾ 5.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p$ and a nonzero integer $n$, let $\nu_p(n)$ denote the $p$-adic valuation of $n$. For $\alpha\in\mathbb{Q}$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}$, define the generalized binomial coefficient $\binom{\alpha}{k}=\prod_{j=1}^{k}\frac{\alpha-j+1}{j}$ (and $\binom{\alpha}{0}=1$). Decide whether all three of the following statements hold.

(i) Let $m\ge 2$ and $r$ be integers with $m>2$, $m\not\equiv r\pmod 2$, and $r\ge -m/2$. For every odd prime $p>r$ not dividing $m$ with $p\equiv r\pmod m$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^{km}\binom{r/m}{k}^{m}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{3}}.$$

(ii) Let $m\ge 2$ and $r$ be integers with $r\ge -m$. For every odd prime $p>r$ not dividing $m$ with $p\equiv r\pmod{2m}$, and for every $n\in\{1,2,\dots,m-1\}$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}(-1)^{k}\binom{r/m}{k}^{2n+1}\equiv 0\pmod{p^{2}}.$$

(iii) For every prime $p$ and every positive integer $n$,
$$\nu_p\!\left(\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\binom{-1/(p+1)}{k}^{p+1}\right)\ \ge\ c_p\,\lfloor \nu_p(n)+1\rfloor,$$
where $c_2=1$, $c_3=3$, and $c_p=5$ for $p\ge 5$.
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this three-part conjecture on supercongruences for sums of powers of generalized binomial coefficients was located. It appears to remain open or with at most partial progress.
